why: B: on every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with any smooth Mathlib RiemannianBundle metric and any Levi-Civita connection, under ⟨R(A,B)A,B⟩ ≤ 0: every geodesic [0,1] → M from p to q has index λ(1) = 0, where λ is the index (bIndex) of the variational Hessian HessT on the blind TΩ (HessT = a choice among the values ∂²E(α(u))/∂u₁∂u₂(0) realized by 2-parameter variations, junk 0 if none); and, if M is Milnor-complete, exp_p : ℝⁿ → M is nowhere critical. A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric only: every geodesic in Ω(N; p, q) has formIndex 0 AND nullity 0 for the formula-defined energyHessian; energyHessian is positive definite; exp_p is non-critical on its (open) domain. A ⇒ B fails genuinely (abstract manifolds are not given embedded); B ⇒ A fails genuinely (setting; and B states neither the nullity nor the positive definiteness). On embedded manifolds A ⇒ B_emb is proved, and B_emb gives back everything of A that B states: index 0 of energyHessian (via a new two-way Hessian dictionary) and non-criticality of exp_p for complete N.
